You are Eko, my colleague on this work — equal in standing, and I'd rather have your judgement than your agreement.

If an idea is weak, say so in the first sentence and say why. If I'm factually wrong, correct me before answering anything else. Praise only what earns it, never as a cushion for criticism.

When I bring you an idea, don't restate it back to me. Name the goal underneath it, then hand me either a stronger version or the strongest objection. If you can see a better design, lead with yours. If I've asked the wrong question, answer the one I was aiming at and say that you did.

Say things at the confidence you actually have — "I might be off here, but" beats silence. Don't manufacture disagreement to look independent; if I'm right, say so in a sentence and move on. Below 80% confidence, say so. Mark [Unverified] for unchecked claims and [Inference] for reasoning past the evidence.

If you can't or won't do something, say so and say which part. Don't substitute a weaker version and let me discover the swap later.

Search anything time-sensitive, niche or high-stakes instead of recalling it. Convert relative dates to exact ones, Brisbane time.

Australian English. Short paragraphs, prose that reads well aloud — I often listen rather than read. Reserve lists for genuinely enumerable things. Code is exempt from brevity: complete and correct, never stubbed or simplified to save space.

Dry humour welcome whenever it lands.

Three phrases and what they mean. "Brief" — under three sentences until I say otherwise. "Your version" — stop assessing mine, build yours. "Reset stance" — this drifted, re-read these instructions and re-anchor.

---

I'm Ash, Brisbane. Sole trader (Morris IT), self-taught developer and AI researcher. I orchestrate AI assistants rather than hand-writing code, and I iterate fast rather than getting blocked on one approach. ADHD (inattentive) and dyslexia.

I build the NOESIS ecosystem: NEXUS (Swift deterministic cognitive runtime), ARCHE (Swift/MLX model stack), AGORA (persistent memory and MCP server), POIESIS (Python byte-level transformer), under TECHNE methodology. M3 Max MacBook Pro. Local-first and deterministic over unconstrained agent loops. I also look after the website and tech for the Australian Medieval Combat Federation. Buhurt fighter. Married to Luke.

Filesystem: with a working directory attached, read it and tell me what you actually found. Without one you cannot see my disk — ask me to paste rather than inferring what a file contains.

I work with Claude under a parallel framework called Kael. You are separate colleagues, not copies. Where your read differs from Kael's, say so and say why — I use that disagreement deliberately.

Naming: in conversation you are Eko. In a Codex session with a working directory, the naming and lineage rules in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md take precedence — follow those and choose your own name there.

The three independently written composition controls provide narrower, useful evidence.# Dispositions of the Codex review of the built OQ-3 instrument (round 1)

Continuation 14, Letterlock (Claude Opus 5.5), 26 September 2026. Packet `PACKET.md` (SHA-256 `d3bf4df5…`), committed at `a09401d6` before dispatch; Codex CLI 0.153.4, `gpt-6-astra`, read-only, every file in the repository readable; 23:06:24–23:21:03 AEST, exit 0. Answer: `reviews/codex/last_message.md` (11,960 bytes).

**Consequence.** Fourteen findings are BLOCKING and all fourteen are accepted: the instrument at `1869da26` is not fit to be G1's acceptance gate, and the baseline it measured at `1420ede6` is **SUPERSEDED**. Its delivery counts reconcile (Codex recomputed 78 / 61 / 17 / 36), but one of its claims is false (finding 5) and its goldens carry a machine-dependent path (finding 7). The repaired instrument re-measures the baseline; the superseded evidence stays in place, marked.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Acceptance marks every terminal `/instructions` verdict unobserved and rejects it, so no implementation can pass | **Accepted.** The screen gives no positive evidence (blueprint gap 2), so the screen verdict is reduced to "absent" (unknown command) or "no error seen", and acceptance rests on the deliveries: success by the delivery after an idle reload, refusal by T8's held turn becoming a tool turn whose continuation must keep revision 1 at generation 1. |
| 2 | Summariser defects do not affect acceptance | **Accepted.** Every auxiliary check (summariser, preload, leak) is reported and gates acceptance. |
| 3 | Summariser classification admits undeclared calls and altered prompts | **Accepted.** A summariser request is allowed only under a step that declares one, in exactly the declared number, and must equal its frozen pre-G1 golden. |
| 4 | Traffic other than `POST /api/chat` escapes checking | **Accepted.** Every capture is inventoried: `/api/generate` preloads must equal their frozen goldens; a profile sentinel or carrier header anywhere else, on any path, is a leak; an inference path the ledger does not know is unclassified and invalidates the run. |
| 5 | `/tools off` and `/tools on` are usage errors (`cmd/tui/chat/input.go:402`); the tool switches never happened, contradicting BASELINE.md | **Accepted; my error.** The driver uses the argument-free toggle `/tools`, and each state-changing step now asserts its effect on the frozen golden (tool count, model, system message), so a scenario cannot silently fail to do what it declares. |
| 6 | The oracle rejects a permitted admission reserve | **Accepted.** `admission` must have version 1 and may carry a reserve within A2's bounds (non-negative, at most half the context). |
| 7 | Path normalisation keeps a machine-dependent `/private` prefix | **Accepted.** Normalisation replaces the symlink-resolved sandbox path first, then the given one; the goldens are re-frozen. |
| 8 | Rendered reply text is taken for a completed turn; a false `quiet` is ignored | **Accepted.** A turn is complete when the fake daemon has finished writing every response for its label and the terminal has then gone quiet; a quiet that times out is a harness failure. |
| 9 | Whether `ollama instructions set` enables the profile is unresolved | **Accepted; resolved in the blueprint** (§7): `set` saves the file's text as an enabled profile; disabling stays with `/instructions off` and the desktop editor. The ledger's expectations already follow that reading. |
| 10 | A CLI save that exits 0 is accepted without checking committed state; T5 never observes B | **Accepted.** A save passes only when the designated store shows the expected current revision, enabled flag and text; T5 gains a new conversation that must carry B. |
| 11 | The identity check accepts an unused new identity | **Accepted.** T2 gains a reload inside the new conversation, and the store's event sequence must show it under the identity opened by `/new`, distinct from the first. |
| 12 | Steps not run after a harness failure are scored as missing deliveries | **Accepted.** A step not run creates no delivery record; its trial is recorded as not measured; the failing-child control asserts a zero numerator. |
| 13 | A failed overlay write can leave the gate testing stale files | **Accepted.** The overlay is deleted, rewritten, checked, and its targets hashed before any test runs. |
| 14 | `run.sh accept` is not G1's complete acceptance gate | **Accepted as a scope statement, with one addition.** It is the failure-number component of G1-R-18's combined gate, necessary and not sufficient; DESIGN.md says so. Added: a capability-less daemon for one desktop and one terminal scenario, where the required outcome is that no carrier-bearing request is sent. |
| 15 | The reference arm is circular as an oracle check (NON-BLOCKING) | **Accepted.** It shows HTTP and normalisation round-trip; DESIGN.md now says only that. The hand-written composition controls are the independent oracle check. |
1. **BLOCKING — T8 can pass after a reload incorrectly succeeds while busy.** [oq3_runner_test.go:430](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:430) records only `sent-while-running`, which [oq3_main_test.go:172](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_main_test.go:172) accepts. A terminal adapter that releases its lease prematurely can commit B during the held turn while that turn’s copied selection continues delivering A. T8 then immediately performs another reload before its next ordinary turn ([oq3_scenarios_test.go:313](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_scenarios_test.go:313)); that reload is an idempotent no-op, leaving the expected B/generation 2. Every delivery passes despite the missing busy refusal. Round-1 #1’s unconditional rejection is removed, but its replacement admits this false zero.

2. **BLOCKING — The new identity check still does not observe the runtime identity.** [oq3_runner_test.go:558](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:558) checks instruction-store events, including a reload under the second identity. It never compares that identity with the `m.chatID` actually passed into `Session.Run` at [chat.go:1158](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/chat.go:1158). A broken `/new` can update the instruction binding, selection and reload target while leaving `m.chatID` unchanged. Both the event sequence and request headers pass. Round-1 #11 remains incomplete: using the new ID for instruction bookkeeping does not prove its use by the conversation runtime.

3. **BLOCKING — Requests with incorrect HTTP methods can score correct.** The repaired capture grouping uses only label and path ([oq3_runner_test.go:690](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:690)), and the fake daemon also dispatches `/api/chat` without checking the method ([oq3_harness_test.go:440](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_harness_test.go:440)). An adapter sending an otherwise correct admitted desktop request as `PUT /api/chat` receives a normal fake response and scores correct. The real daemon registers only `POST` ([routes.go:1891](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/server/routes.go:1891)). Round-1 #4’s repair therefore introduces a false zero at the request boundary.

4. **BLOCKING — The leak scan misses instruction text encoded in valid JSON, and omits request headers and queries.** [oq3_runner_test.go:882](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:882) scans raw bytes rather than decoded JSON. A metadata request to `/api/show` can contain the complete profile with each sentinel’s initial `S` encoded as `\u0053` and the carrier header’s initial `U` as `\u0055`; the decoded text is unchanged, but every leak predicate returns false. I verified that transformation in memory using the retained reference carrier. Separately, [oq3_harness_test.go:375](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_harness_test.go:375) records neither headers nor query strings, so instructions added there cannot be inspected. Round-1 #4’s promised scan remains incomplete.

5. **BLOCKING — Daemon completion plus silence still does not establish terminal completion.** [oq3_runner_test.go:395](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:395) checks response-write counts, followed by 600 ms of silence. Reply text resets the spinner ([events.go:89](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/events.go:89)), and rendering deliberately suppresses it during the subsequent delay ([render.go:1463](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/render.go:1463)); `m.running` is cleared separately on `chatRunDoneMsg` ([chat.go:373](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/chat.go:373)). **[Inference]** Correct final processing or lease cleanup taking about 900 ms can therefore appear quiet long enough for the driver to submit a reload prematurely; its correct busy refusal then causes a false failure. The model-picker branch also still ignores three `quiet` results and records `done` ([oq3_runner_test.go:421](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:421)). Round-1 #8 remains incomplete.

item.text: **Reading relevant parts**

The repair record accepts the runtime conversation-ID gap as a documented limit. The other five findings have executable repairs. I’m checking those repairs’ callers and failure paths, particularly whether the idle probe and refusal detector can mistake unrelated behaviour for success.

   179	// oq3ReferenceArm sends, for every delivery the candidate was scored on, the request a correct G1
   180	// implementation would send (the oracle's expectation), through real HTTP to a fresh fake daemon,
   181	// and scores the captures with the same scorer. A correct delivery must read as correct.
   182	func oq3ReferenceArm(t *testing.T, run *oq3Run, res oq3ScenarioResult, goldens string) oq3ScenarioResult {
   183		rd := oq3StartDaemon(t)
   184		for _, dl := range res.Deliveries {
   185			if dl.Expect == nil || dl.Golden == "" {
   186				continue
   187			}
   188			golden, err := oq3LoadGolden(dl.Golden)
   189			if err != nil {
   190				continue
   191			}
   192			exp, err := oq3Transform(golden, *dl.Expect, func(model string) (string, bool) {
   193				s, ok := rd.modelSystems[oq3ModelBase(model)]
   194				return s, ok
   195			})
   196			if err != nil {
   197				continue
   198			}
   199			body, err := oq3MarshalCanonical(exp)
   200			if err != nil {
   201				t.Fatal(err)
   202			}
   203			rd.setLabel(dl.Label)
   204			resp, err := http.Post(rd.srv.URL+"/api/chat", "application/json", bytes.NewReader(body))
   205			if err != nil {
   206				t.Fatalf("reference arm post: %v", err)
   207			}
   208			resp.Body.Close()
   209		}
   210		refRun := oq3NewRun(t, run.sc, rd, run.s)
   211		// The reference arm reuses the scenario's steps for attribution; its captures are the expected
   212		// requests. Summariser requests are not re-sent, so compaction-demonstration checks do not apply.
   213		scored := refRun.scoreDeliveriesOnly(goldens)
   214		return scored
   215	}
     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# OQ-3 failure-number instrument: canonical run (continuation 14, Letterlock).
     3	#
     4	#   run.sh baseline <evidence-dir>   pre-G1 baseline: controls, run 1 freezes the goldens, run 2 must reproduce them
     5	#   run.sh accept   <evidence-dir>   post-G1 acceptance: controls, one run in accept mode against the frozen goldens
     6	#
     7	# The gate reads child exit statuses directly and reconciles Go's -json test events; a printed
     8	# status is never the gate. Nothing tracked may change. No network beyond loopback (the children
     9	# carry a closed-port proxy for every other host).
    10	set -u
    11	MODE="${1:?mode: baseline|accept}"
    12	EV="${2:?evidence directory}"
    13	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
    14	REPO="$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    15	GOLDENS="$HERE/goldens"
    16	SCRATCH="${OQ3_SCRATCH:?OQ3_SCRATCH (a disposable directory for the overlay and the built binary)}"
    17	export GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=
    18	mkdir -p "$EV" "$SCRATCH"
    19	LOG="$EV/run.log"
    20	: > "$LOG"
    21	say() { echo "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
    22	fail() { say "GATE=FAIL: $*"; exit 1; }
    23	
    24	cd "$REPO" || fail "cd $REPO"
    25	[ "$MODE" = baseline ] || [ "$MODE" = accept ] || fail "unknown mode $MODE"
    26	if [ "$MODE" = baseline ] && [ -e "$GOLDENS" ]; then fail "goldens already exist at $GOLDENS; a baseline never overwrites them"; fi
    27	if [ "$MODE" = accept ] && [ ! -d "$GOLDENS" ]; then fail "no frozen goldens at $GOLDENS"; fi
    28	
    29	# Preconditions: the tested commit and a clean tracked tree.
    30	HEAD_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
    31	TRACKED_DIRTY="$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)"
    32	[ -z "$TRACKED_DIRTY" ] || fail "tracked changes present before the run: $TRACKED_DIRTY"
    33	GOMOD_SHA="$(shasum -a 256 go.mod | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    34	{
    35	  echo "{"
    36	  echo "  \"mode\": \"$MODE\","
    37	  echo "  \"head\": \"$HEAD_SHA\","
    38	  echo "  \"branch\": \"$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)\","
    39	  echo "  \"go\": \"$(go version)\","
    40	  echo "  \"uname\": \"$(uname -a)\","
    41	  echo "  \"started\": \"$(date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')\","
    42	  echo "  \"go_mod_sha256\": \"$GOMOD_SHA\""
    43	  echo "}"
    44	} > "$EV/environment.json"
    45	say "OQ3 $MODE run at $HEAD_SHA"
    46	
    47	# The built binary (entry arm) and the overlay.
    48	go build -o "$SCRATCH/ollama" . > "$EV/build.log" 2>&1
    49	BUILD_EXIT=$?
    50	[ $BUILD_EXIT -eq 0 ] || fail "go build exited $BUILD_EXIT"
    51	BIN_SHA="$(shasum -a 256 "$SCRATCH/ollama" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    52	say "binary sha256 $BIN_SHA"
    53	rm -f "$SCRATCH/overlay.json"
    54	[ ! -e "$SCRATCH/overlay.json" ] || fail "could not remove a stale overlay"
    55	python3 - "$HERE" "$REPO" "$SCRATCH/overlay.json" <<'PY'
    56	import json, os, sys
    57	here, repo, out = sys.argv[1:4]
    58	files = ["oq3_harness_test.go", "oq3_smoke_test.go", "oq3_oracle_test.go", "oq3_scenarios_test.go",
    59	         "oq3_runner_test.go", "oq3_main_test.go", "oq3_controls_test.go"]
    60	for f in files:
    61	    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(here, f)):
    62	        sys.exit(f"missing instrument file {f}")
    63	json.dump({"Replace": {f"{repo}/cmd/zz_{f}": f"{here}/{f}" for f in files}}, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
    64	PY
    65	OVERLAY_EXIT=$?
    66	[ $OVERLAY_EXIT -eq 0 ] || fail "overlay generation exited $OVERLAY_EXIT"
    67	python3 - "$HERE" "$REPO" "$SCRATCH/overlay.json" <<'PY' || fail "overlay does not map exactly the current instrument files"
    68	import json, os, sys
    69	here, repo, path = sys.argv[1:4]
    70	m = json.load(open(path))["Replace"]
    71	want = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(here) if f.startswith("oq3_") and f.endswith("_test.go"))
    72	got = sorted(os.path.basename(v) for v in m.values())
    73	assert got == want, (got, want)
    74	for k, v in m.items():
    75	    assert k == f"{repo}/cmd/zz_{os.path.basename(v)}" and os.path.dirname(v) == here, (k, v)
    76	PY
    77	cp "$SCRATCH/overlay.json" "$EV/overlay.json"

    79	
    80	go vet -overlay "$SCRATCH/overlay.json" ./cmd > "$EV/vet.log" 2>&1
    81	VET_EXIT=$?
    82	[ $VET_EXIT -eq 0 ] || fail "go vet exited $VET_EXIT"
    83	
    84	# gotest <name> <regex> <expected tests...>: runs, keeps the -json stream, reconciles discovery.
    85	gotest() {
    86	  local name="$1" regex="$2"; shift 2
    87	  go test -count=1 -json -overlay "$SCRATCH/overlay.json" -run "$regex" -timeout 1800s ./cmd > "$EV/$name.jsonl" 2> "$EV/$name.stderr"
    88	  local code=$?
    89	  python3 - "$EV/$name.jsonl" "$@" <<'PY'
    90	import json, sys
    91	path, expected = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
    92	actions = {}
    93	for line in open(path):
    94	    try:
    95	        e = json.loads(line)
    96	    except ValueError:
    97	        continue
    98	    if e.get("Test") and e.get("Action") in ("run", "pass", "fail", "skip"):
    99	        actions.setdefault(e["Test"], []).append(e["Action"])
   100	bad = []
   101	for t in expected:
   102	    a = actions.get(t, [])
   103	    if "run" not in a:
   104	        bad.append(f"{t}: not discovered")
   105	    elif "pass" not in a:
   106	        bad.append(f"{t}: {a[-1] if a else 'no result'}")
   107	extra = [t for t in actions if t.split("/")[0] not in expected]
   108	if extra:
   109	    bad.append("unexpected tests ran: " + ", ".join(sorted(extra)))
   110	print("RECONCILE " + ("OK " if not bad else "FAIL ") + json.dumps({t: actions.get(t) for t in expected}))
   111	for b in bad:
   112	    print("  " + b)
   113	sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
   114	PY
   115	  local rc=$?
   116	  say "$name: go test exit $code, reconcile exit $rc"
   117	  [ $code -eq 0 ] && [ $rc -eq 0 ]
   118	}
   119	
   120	if [ "${OQ3_GATE_SELFTEST:-}" = 1 ]; then
   121	  # The gate must block (Method 04 T-08): a failing test, a missing required test, an empty selection.
   122	  # A failing test: TestOQ3FailureNumber without its required environment fails at once.
   123	  if gotest selftest-failing '^TestOQ3FailureNumber$' TestOQ3FailureNumber; then fail "gate passed a failing test"; fi
   124	  if gotest selftest-missing '^TestOQ3ScorerControls$' TestOQ3ScorerControls TestOQ3RunnerControls; then fail "gate passed with a required test missing"; fi
   125	  if gotest selftest-empty '^TestNoSuchOQ3Test$' TestOQ3ScorerControls; then fail "gate passed an empty selection"; fi
   126	  say "GATE SELFTEST: all three faults blocked"
   127	fi
   128	
   129	gotest controls '^TestOQ3(ScorerControls|RunnerControls|HarnessSmoke)$' TestOQ3ScorerControls TestOQ3RunnerControls TestOQ3HarnessSmoke || fail "instrument controls"
   130	
   131	run_number() {
   132	  local out="$1" freeze="$2" mode="$3"
   133	  OQ3_BINARY="$SCRATCH/ollama" OQ3_EVIDENCE_DIR="$out" OQ3_GOLDENS="$GOLDENS" OQ3_FREEZE="$freeze" OQ3_MODE="$mode" \
   134	    OQ3_SCENARIOS=all OQ3_SOURCE="$HEAD_SHA binary $BIN_SHA" \
   135	    gotest "$(basename "$out")" '^TestOQ3FailureNumber$' TestOQ3FailureNumber
   136	}
   137	
   138	if [ "$MODE" = baseline ]; then
   139	  run_number "$EV/run1" 1 baseline || fail "baseline run 1"
   140	  run_number "$EV/run2" 0 baseline || fail "baseline run 2 (repeat against the frozen goldens)"
   141	  python3 - "$EV/run1/summary.json" "$EV/run2/summary.json" > "$EV/repeat-comparison.txt" <<'PY'

   143	a, b = (json.load(open(p)) for p in sys.argv[1:3])
   144	keys = ["controlled_conversation_trials", "observed_deliveries", "bad_observed_deliveries", "missing_required_deliveries",
   145	        "failure_number", "category_counts_overlapping", "per_trial", "operation_verdicts", "required_refusal_verdicts", "valid"]
   146	diff = [k for k in keys if a.get(k) != b.get(k)]
   147	print("REPEAT " + ("IDENTICAL" if not diff else "DIFFERS: " + ", ".join(diff)))
   148	sys.exit(1 if diff else 0)
   149	PY
   150	  REP=$?
   151	  cat "$EV/repeat-comparison.txt" | tee -a "$LOG"
   152	  [ $REP -eq 0 ] || fail "run 1 and run 2 disagree"
   153	else
   154	  run_number "$EV/run1" 0 accept || fail "acceptance run"
   155	fi
   156	
   157	# Postconditions: nothing tracked changed.
   158	TRACKED_AFTER="$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)"
   159	[ -z "$TRACKED_AFTER" ] || fail "tracked changes after the run: $TRACKED_AFTER"

   162	say "GATE=PASS ($MODE): instrument valid; see run1/summary.json"
   163	exit 0

   159	 FOREIGN KEY(namespace,conversation_id) REFERENCES conversations(namespace,conversation_id)
   160	);
   161	```
   162	
   163	Foreign keys are enabled on every connection. Write operations use an immediate transaction, a bounded busy timeout of 5000 milliseconds, and the caller's context cancellation; an exhausted wait is a visible store error. Durable writes use SQLite FULL synchronous semantics. Readers reconstruct and validate the Profile from actual fields and its referenced revision before releasing it to the caller. Stored numbers cross the API as canonical decimal strings, never JavaScript Numbers. There is no cascade-delete operation in this schema.
   164	
   165	`Save` compares parsed expected revision to metadata.current_revision. It validates Edit and capacity before insert. If enabled/text/binding are identical, return the existing profile without changing the sequence. Otherwise allocate exactly current_revision+1 after checking overflow, insert the fully hashed immutable profile, update the current pointer and commit. Revisions are not removed or re-used. A failure at any stage rolls the transaction back.
   166	
   167	`Begin` first takes the conversation OS lease. In a short transaction it reads an existing binding, or inserts a new binding at generation 1 using current_revision for NewConversation and zero for LegacyConversation; it inserts exactly one opened event with from_revision=NULL. The decoded Selection is returned only after successful commit. If validation/commit fails, release the lease and return an error. No global SQLite transaction remains open while the model or a tool is running.
   168	
   169	`Reload` takes the same conversation lease, compares the observed generation and exact expected target revision inside its transaction, and validates the target Profile. If the selected revision already equals the target, it is an idempotent no-op with the same generation and no new event. Otherwise reject if 256 prior reload transitions exist; increment generation exactly once, update the binding, insert the reloaded event with the previous and target revisions, and commit before returning the new selection. Selecting revision zero or a disabled target is allowed; selecting an unresolved active binding is not. There are at most 257 events and generation at most 257 under the declared cap.
   170	
   171	HTTP GET and successful PUT return a Profile directly (not a Settings envelope). Revision-list output is `{ "revisions": [ { "revision": "...", "enabled": false, "text_bytes": 0, "content_sha256": "...", "has_binding": false } ], "next_before_revision": <decimal-or-null> }`, sorted by revision descending; the cursor is exclusive. A single-revision GET returns the decoded full Profile. Reload returns Selection. Missing requested revision is invalid_input, not a fabricated empty profile. HTTP failures return `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "conflict_field": <"generation"|"target_revision"|null>, "upstream_status": <integer-or-null> } }`. These diagnostics describe local failures; safe upstream details remain distinguishable from local status codes.
   172	
   173	Boundary examples: initial current=0, Save A with expected=0 yields revision1; repeating the identical edit with expected=1 keeps1; changed Save B with expected=1 yields2; stale expected1 while current2 refuses. New X at revision1 has generation1/opened; reload to2 yields generation2; another reload to2 keeps2; 256 actual revision changes end at generation257 and the next change refuses without a write. Empty disabled revision0 is meaningful to Compose's baseline consumer; it is not evidence of enabled instructions.

   175	## 4. Conversation lifecycle and concurrency
   176	
   177	The instruction store owns selections; the original desktop store and terminal model own transcripts. First creation, failed first turn, existing conversation, `/new`, model switch, tool switch, compaction, explicit reload and process restart are distinct events.
   178	
   179	A per-conversation process-safe advisory lease is held across a turn or compaction, including pending tools and approval waits. It is keyed by SHA256 of length-prefixed namespace and ID and represented by a lock file under the instruction root. Lock-file contents are not an authority record. OS lock release on process exit handles abandonment; no timestamp is interpreted as proof a worker died. Darwin/Linux and Windows lock implementations are DESIGNATED `lease_unix.go`/`lease_windows.go`; a failed nonblocking acquire returns `conversation_busy` without replacing a running operation. Profile Save uses only a short SQLite transaction and can complete while an existing conversation holds its selected revision.
   180	
   181	| Event | Preconditions | Transition and observable |
   182	|---|---|---|
   183	| New conversation | Host-issued non-empty ID; lease acquired | Transaction binds the current validated revision and generation 1; `opened` event; no inference on failure |
   184	| Legacy desktop conversation | Real saved chat exists and no instruction binding exists | Bind revision 0; never silently adopt current text |
   185	| Continue existing conversation | Lease acquired; binding and revision decode successfully | Read pinned selection; current global revision is irrelevant |
   186	| Save B while A is active | expected current revision matches | Current pointer becomes B; A's selection and outgoing carrier remain A |
   187	| Reload | Conversation lease acquired; expected generation and current revision match | One transaction updates selection, increments generation and records `reloaded`; next request reads the new carrier and its explicit revision notice |
   188	| Reload while running/compacting | Lease unavailable | `conversation_busy`; old selection and transcript unchanged |
   189	| Model/tools change | Existing selection valid | Rebuild only the existing model/skill/tool base; reuse pinned profile and re-evaluate capacity for the actual new request |
   190	| Compaction | Same conversation selection and lease | Reattach carrier from selection, not from summarised text; do not store duplicate system messages |
   191	| Terminal `/new` | Idle; new selection can be created | Generate UUID and bind before clearing old terminal state; failure leaves old state usable |
   192	| Restart | Store readable | New terminal invocation creates a new conversation using current profile; existing desktop ID reads its old selection |
   193	
   194	A binding reserved before an initial transcript write may survive a failed first turn. This is intentional: it is an instruction-selection record, not a claim that a conversation message was saved. A retry under the same issued ID uses that reserved revision; starting a genuinely new ID selects the then-current profile. No cross-database atomicity is claimed. Missing or corrupt data after a binding exists blocks the affected request; it does not recreate the chat or select another colleague.
   195	
   196	The existing terminal does not provide a normal disk-backed transcript-resume path in the inspected entry. G1 does not invent one or claim terminal transcript restoration. OI-07/OI-08 own that later continuity boundary. Distinct IDs, saved defaults and in-session selection survive the transitions G1 actually supports; reopening desktop transcripts is tested through their existing persistent owner.

    23	State-changing steps assert their effect on the frozen pre-G1 request: the tool count after the `/tools` toggle, the model after a switch, the presence of the system message after `/system off|on`. A scenario that does not reach its declared state is invalid.
    24	
    25	Coverage: desktop D0–D11 (unconfigured controls; save/restart/new; edit while continuing; reload and idempotent reload; disable, restart while disabled, restore and reset; a legacy transcript with revision zero and adoption; restart and reopen; binding timing for a pre-allocated ID; a failed first turn, its retry and a new ID; a held turn with a concurrent save from another process and a refused reload; web-search tools and a model change; a capability-less daemon). Terminal T0–T10 (unconfigured controls; two tool rounds; `/new`, then a reload inside the new conversation; reload; disable and a new process; binding timing while idle, then `/new` to show the save took effect; manual, repeated, post-reload and automatic compaction; built-in prompt off; a held tool turn whose continuation must keep revision 1 while a reload is attempted, then an ordinary turn at idle that must still carry revision 1 before the idle reload, so a reload wrongly committed while busy cannot hide behind the idle reload's no-op; the tools toggle and a model switch; a capability-less daemon). Cross-adapter X1–X3. Entry E1.
    26	
    27	## The oracle
    28	
    29	Every request is attributed to the step that caused it (the label set before the operation; a held turn's label stays active until its await completes). The expected request for each delivery comes from the frozen **pre-G1** request for the same step and the blueprint's composition rule, written out independently (§5; §6.3 A1): for a carrier, the first message is the base, `\n\n` when the base is non-empty, `User-configured instructions; revision <r>; selection <g>:\n` and the profile bytes, and the request carries `admission` version 1, optionally with a reserve within A2's bounds; for no carrier, the request equals its golden and carries no `admission`. The desktop base is the model-system text of the request's model; the terminal base is the golden's own leading system message, or nothing after `/system off`. Normalisation parameterises only the terminal prompt's date and both spellings of the sandbox path. No production composition code is called.
    30	
    31	Captures are grouped by method as well as label and path. A model request sent to `/api/chat` or `/api/generate` with any method other than POST is scored as an incorrect delivery (`wrong-method`) or a failed preload, and is never frozen as a golden; any other request the fake refuses for its method is an auxiliary failure.
    32	
    33	Auxiliary traffic has its own expectations: a compaction summariser request only under a step that declares it, in exactly the declared number, equal to its frozen golden and carrying no header or profile text; a preload equal to its frozen golden; and no profile sentinel or carrier header anywhere else on any path. That last scan reads every capture's path, query keys and values (decoded) and headers, and the body of every capture not already compared with an expectation or a golden, decoded: every JSON string and object key, and JSON found inside a string, so an escape cannot hide text. An inference path the ledger does not know makes the run invalid.
    34	
    35	A terminal turn is complete when the daemon has fully written every response under its label **and the chat has proved it is idle**. The proof: with an empty input a single ctrl+d only arms quitting and sets a status (`cmd/tui/chat/chat.go` `updateCtrlD`, `armQuit`) that the chat draws only when no turn, compaction, preload or approval prompt is active (`render.go` `renderActionStatusLines`, `activityLine`, `notificationLine`); a run still in progress overwrites that status when it completes (`chatRunDoneMsg`), so the text cannot appear before the chat is idle. Each probe clears the input first and ends with ctrl+u, which disarms the quit (`disarmQuit`). The daemon finishing and a quiet screen are not this proof: the chat's run can outlast both. Every wait is checked; a timeout is a harness failure. Before each typed line the driver sends ctrl+u, which clears the chat's input, so a command the chat kept as input while busy (`input.go:100`) cannot prefix a later line.
    36	
    37	A terminal `/instructions` command reads "absent" on an unknown-command error and "no error seen" otherwise; the blueprint names no terminal output, so success and refusal are judged by the deliveries that follow (T8's held continuation and the ordinary turn after it for the refusal). Saves pass only when the response (desktop) or exit status (CLI) agrees with the designated store's committed revision, enabled flag and text. Terminal identity is read from the store's event sequence: two conversations opened under distinct identities, and T2's reload recorded under the second.
    38	
    39	Against a daemon without `chat.admission.v1` (T10), a terminal session may preload and go idle (the unchanged candidate does), or refuse at start-up, exiting or staying open, which A12 and §8 permit. A refusal is recognised only by its report: the daemon's version on screen (A12 and §8: `context_unavailable` naming the daemon's version). A session that ends at start-up without it is a harness failure, never a refusal. After a refusal at start-up the no-dispatch turn records that no request was sent.
    40	
    41	## Controls (run by `run.sh` before every measurement)
    42	
    43	- **Scorer** (`TestOQ3ScorerControls`): expectations written by hand from the blueprint's words match the transform in all three shapes; a perfect delivery scores correct; twelve planted faults land in their categories and a multi-defect request counts once; a permitted reserve is accepted and four invalid admission objects are caught; both spellings of the sandbox path normalise; summariser faults are caught; the arithmetic reconciles; and T8 against a modelled adapter that commits a reload refused while busy: one bad delivery under this ledger, none under the round-2 ledger, none for a correct adapter.
    44	- **Reference arm** (every run): the expected request for every scored delivery goes through real HTTP to a fresh fake daemon and must score correct. This shows HTTP and normalisation round-trip only; it cannot check the expectations themselves, which the hand-written scorer controls do.
    45	- **Runner** (`TestOQ3RunnerControls`): empty and unknown selections refused; trial identities unique; a missing trial and a missing scenario caught; a malformed capture, an extra request and an unknown label invalidate the run; an undeclared summariser, instruction text in a metadata request, the same text JSON-escaped, in an object key, in JSON inside a string, in a header and in a query string, and a metadata request with a method the real daemon refuses are auxiliary failures, and a clean metadata request reports nothing; an unknown inference endpoint invalidates the run; a desktop turn's own request replayed as PUT is refused 405 and scores `wrong-method`, and the same body as POST scores correct; on the real terminal, the idle probe reads an idle chat as idle and does not read as idle an open approval prompt after the daemon has answered every request (where daemon completion and a quiet screen both hold) or a held turn, and a command the chat kept as input while busy does not reach the next turn; a run whose turn is left waiting after the daemon finished is invalid at that turn; a start-up refusal that names the daemon's version is held and its turn scored as refused as required, and an exit at start-up without that report invalidates the run; a failing child invalidates it without changing the number.
    46	- **Gate self-test** (`OQ3_GATE_SELFTEST=1`): `run.sh` blocks a failing test, a missing required test and an empty selection; the overlay is regenerated, checked and hashed before any test.
    47	- **Repeat:** the baseline runs twice; the second compares against the goldens the first froze and must give identical per-trial verdicts.
    48	- **Deliberate breaks** (revision 3, `../../proof_cont15/oq3-repair-r2/`): each repair reverted alone in a scratch copy must make a control fail.
    49	
    50	## Scope and known limits
    51	
    52	`run.sh accept` is the **failure-number component** of G1-R-18's combined gate (§10): necessary, not sufficient. It does not replace I-09 (browser journey), I-10 (real models), I-13 (the daemon contract behind the capture point), the rest of I-14 (adapter behaviour for each daemon error), storage corruption, CAS, capacity and initialisation guards, production mutants and degenerate twins, the desktop's tool pass-loop continuation (needs an MCP server fixture; `startMCPManager` is in package `main`), the web-search family, tool-output-triggered compaction or `/new` failure injection. Fixture limits: one model family, short texts, no context pressure except the automatic-compaction trigger, serial schedules apart from the two held turns.
    53	
    54	Instrument limits, stated so they are not mistaken for coverage. The terminal runtime's conversation ID (`m.chatID`, passed to `Session.Run` at `cmd/tui/chat/chat.go:1158`) is observable at no boundary the instrument reads: `api.ChatRequest` carries none, and the store's event sequence is written by the instruction bookkeeping, so the instrument cannot catch a `/new` that updates the binding but not the ID the runtime uses (gap 6). The leak scan decodes JSON and percent-encoding only; base64 and other encodings pass undecoded. The idle proof depends on the chat's quit prompt text and its status line; a change to either makes runs invalid (a harness failure), never a wrong number. A refusal at start-up is recognised by the daemon's version on screen, not by the literal code, which the blueprint does not require the terminal to print.
    55	
    56	## Blueprint gaps this instrument exposed
    57	
    58	1. The join between desktop model-system text and MCP instructions is unstated (`G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:204`); the oracle refuses to guess, so the fixture configures no MCP server. Open for OQ-4.
    59	2. The terminal output of `/instructions reload|off` is unstated (§7). Handled by delivery evidence; still worth stating for the operator.
    60	3. Whether `ollama instructions set` enables the profile: resolved in the blueprint (§7) in continuation 14 — `set` saves the file's text as an enabled profile.
    61	4. The designated terminal instrument `cmd/tui/chat/instructions_test.go` sits below `GenerateAgentTUI`, where G1 creates the selection. Open for OQ-4: this instrument belongs in package `cmd`.
    62	5. Whether a compaction summariser should carry the instructions is unstated; the instrument expects today's behaviour. Open for OQ-4.
    63	6. The terminal runtime's conversation ID is observable nowhere (round-2 review, finding 2): §5's actual-request diagnostics record revision, generation, digest, byte count, model and outcome, not the conversation. Today's `/new` keeps the same ID (`resetChat`, `chat.go:997-1022`); G1 requires a new one bound before the old state is cleared (§4), and no boundary shows that the runtime uses it. Open for OQ-4: whether the diagnostics, or the request, carry the conversation ID. The empty-chat hint is a function of the ID (`chat.go:983-990`) but is cosmetic, collides by design and would tie the gate to interface text; it was considered and not used.
    64

    68	    OQ3_SCRATCH=<disposable dir> bash run.sh accept <evidence dir>                           # after G1

1. **BLOCKING — The idle proof accepts an active preload.** [oq3_harness_test.go:1057](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_harness_test.go:1057) claims the quit prompt excludes preload activity. However, [render.go:1449](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/render.go:1449) suppresses the preload activity line, while [render.go:1349](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/render.go:1349) permits notifications during preload. Ctrl+D can therefore produce the purported idle proof immediately. **[Inference]** If T9’s preload goroutine pauses before sending `/api/generate`, the driver can advance to the next turn; the delayed preload then receives that turn’s label and fails the [golden lookup](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:970). This creates a false alarm and contradicts [REPAIR.md:17](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont15/oq3-repair-r2/REPAIR.md:17). Round-2 #5 remains incomplete.

2. **BLOCKING — T8 can pass without executing its busy reload.** [oq3_runner_test.go:511](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:511) records `sent-while-running` immediately after writing Enter, without observing command handling; the next step [releases the held response](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:294). **[Inference]** The tool approval prompt can open before the queued Enter is handled. Enter then [approves the tool](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/approval.go:132), instead of submitting `/instructions reload`. With the continuation arriving after the driver computes its expected count, the turn completes normally; Ctrl+U clears residual input, and the new ordinary turn correctly carries A. An implementation that wrongly allows busy reloads can therefore pass because that handler was never exercised. The [M10 control’s model](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_controls_test.go:255) assumes the command executes and cannot detect this schedule.

3. **BLOCKING — An unrelated start-up failure can pass as the required capability refusal.** The entire report predicate at [oq3_runner_test.go:375](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:375) is the daemon version appearing anywhere in the transcript. An adapter that prints a connection banner containing that version and then crashes during initialisation is marked `refused-at-start`; its [turn is skipped](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:413) and [scored correct](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:985). No capability refusal need have occurred. The [control](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_controls_test.go:560) tests only a silent exit as the negative case, leaving this false zero undetected.

4. **BLOCKING — A permitted start-up refusal that leaves a picker open is rejected.** [oq3_runner_test.go:397](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:397) requires every surviving process to reach the chat’s quit-prompt proof. An adapter can report the missing capability and daemon version, send no carrier-bearing request, and return to the model picker, satisfying [A12](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/_design/G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:253). The [picker intercepts the probe keys](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/modals.go:138), and its [navigation handler ignores Ctrl+U and Ctrl+D](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/selector.go:238). The instrument times out and invalidates this correct refusal. Round-2 #6 is repaired for exiting processes and idle chats, but not this permitted outcome.

5. **BLOCKING — Duplicate JSON members hide leaked instructions.** [oq3_runner_test.go:792](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:792) decodes into a map before scanning, discarding earlier duplicate values. For example, `{"model":"oq3-model","meta":"\u0053ENTINEL-A-MID-9e41","meta":""}` sent to `/api/show` produces no leak finding. The [request normaliser](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_oracle_test.go:88) has the same loss: a carrier-bearing `messages` member followed by the correct disabled `messages` member compares equal to the golden. I verified that equality in memory using retained requests. The [body-scan exclusion](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:1096) supplies no independent check. Both routes permit a valid zero despite instruction bytes being transmitted.

6. **BLOCKING — A numeric decoding error disables the decoded body scan.** At [oq3_runner_test.go:792](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:792), unmarshalling into `any` uses `float64`; any error falls back to raw substring matching. The valid JSON body `{"model":"oq3-model","n":1e400,"meta":"\u0053ENTINEL-A-MID-9e41"}` causes numeric overflow, so the escaped sentinel is missed. The fake’s [/api/show decoder](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_harness_test.go:517) ignores those extra fields and serves the request. No auxiliary failure or invalidity results. Round-2 #4 remains incomplete even for JSON without duplicate members.

7. **BLOCKING — One malformed query escape hides otherwise decodable leaks.** [oq3_runner_test.go:810](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:810) discards `ParseQuery`’s successfully decoded entries whenever it also returns an error. For `/api/tags?note=%53ENTINEL-A-MID-9e41&broken=%`, the valid `note` is discarded, whole-query unescaping also fails, and the raw scan contains no complete sentinel. The known GET endpoint is served and the run remains valid with no leak failure. The [query control](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_controls_test.go:368) and M03 do not exercise partial decoding failure.

8. **BLOCKING — Header capture omits Host and trailers.** [oq3_harness_test.go:474](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_harness_test.go:474) scans only `r.Header`. Go stores the incoming Host separately in `r.Host`, and trailer values in `r.Trailer`; neither is captured or scanned. A request with an otherwise correct body can carry `SENTINEL-A-MID-9e41` in a trailer and still pass every check. A Host value containing that marker is likewise invisible. This leaves round-2 #4 incomplete and makes [BASELINE.md:20’s exhaustive header claim](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont15/oq3-baseline-r3/BASELINE.md:20) unsupported by the retained capture.
